question: The height of a trapezium is 68 cm, and the sum of its parallel sides is 75 cm. If the area of the trapezium is (6)/(17) times of the area of a square, then the length of the diagonal of the square is: (Take sqrt2 = 1.41)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of trapezium = ½ × Sum of parallel sides × height = ½ × 75 × 68 = 2550 cm².

Given, Area of trapezium = 6/17 × Area of square.

We know, Area of square can be written as ½ × (Diagonal)².

⇒ 2550 = 6/17 × (½ × d²) = 3/17 × d²

⇒ d² = (2550 × 17) ÷ 3 = 850 × 17 = 14450

⇒ d = √14450 = 85√2 = 85 × 1.41 = 119.85 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 119.85 cm.**
